title: Add attribute-scoped operator RBAC v2 and configurable region-pin audit retention
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce attribute-scoped operator RBAC v2 and per-region audit retention configuration. Backwards-compatible; installers will opt-in via new values. Includes migration job to tag recent audit events for retention grouping.
description:
Motivation:
Operators and managed services running in private deployments require finer-grained RBAC that is aware of the operator's intended region/zone and the data residency constraints of a tenant. At the same time, compliance teams have requested the ability to pin audit retention windows by region (shorter retention for ephemeral operator telemetry, longer for sovereign-region audit records).

This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) attribute-scoped operator RBAC v2 support in the installer to emit operator attributes into the policy decision context, and (2) a configurable region-pin audit retention decorator that tags audit events with retention TTLs derived from tenant and operator attributes. The design keeps default behavior unchanged unless the new configuration is enabled.

High-level changes:
- Installer: add operator attribute configuration (operator.scope, operator.region_hint) and an RBAC policy generation step that produces attribute-bound roles.
- RBAC v2: extend the policy template to accept operator attributes and produce decisions scoped to operator.attributes.region_pin and operator.attributes.allowed_actions.
- Audit subsystem: retention_decorator that enriches audit events with a "region_pin" label and retention_ttl seconds based on merged tenant+operator policy heuristics.
- Backfill/migration: a one-off job (audit-backfill-tag) that scans audit logs from the last 90 days and applies region_pin labels where traceable; safe to run multiple times.
- Docs & values: add installer values sample and upgrade guidance.

Why this is different: most earlier work enforced KMS region pinning or added service-level residency gates. This change ties operator identity attributes to runtime policy decisions and to downstream audit retention classification so that compliance can reason about how long events must be kept depending on the region of origin.

Config example (values.yaml snippet):
installer:
  operatorAttributes:
    operatorId: "ops-rotating-01"
    regionHint: "eu-west-1"
    allowedActions:
      - kms:Encrypt
      - kms:Decrypt
auditRetention:
  default_ttl_days: 30
  region_pins:
    eu: 365
    us: 180
    apac: 90
  operator_overrides:
    ops-rotating-01: 14

Migration notes:
- The migration job audit-backfill-tag is included under tools/migrations. Running it is recommended before turning on region-based retention enforcement. It tags events with "region_pin" metadata and a suggested ttl.
- Existing audit consumers are unchanged; the decorator only adds metadata fields (region_pin, retention_ttl_seconds).

Operational concerns and safeguards:
- Default safe-mode: if a region pin cannot be resolved, events fall back to default_ttl_days.
- No automatic deletion: the installer does not perform deletions; retention_ttl_seconds is advisory and surfaced to downstream retention pipelines which must be configured by SRE/compliance.
- KMS impact: RBAC attribute checks are orthogonal to KMS key selection; operator attributes are used to gate requests but we do not automatically remap keys in this change. A follow-up will add KMS key origin assertions for auto-routing.

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Feature gated behind installer flag (values.installer.operatorAttributes.enabled).
- Canary rollout: enable in a single private deployment region and verify audit metadata, then broaden.

Related tickets: ENG-10234 (RBAC attribute support), SEC-497 (audit retention policy requirements).

notes_for_ops: After upgrade: enable operatorAttributes.enabled in values.yaml, run tools/migrations/audit-backfill-tag --since=90d --rate=1000 to pre-tag events, then enable auditRetention.region_pins. Monitor metrics: audit.decorator.tags_applied, migration.bytes_processed, migration.idempotency_errors.
